description: Use this when someone asks for trending TikTok hashtags, or which hashtags to use, for a niche or topic. Input: a niche or topic in plain words (for example skincare, gym, meal prep). Returns the hashtags used by 2 or more stored public posts from 2 or more creators in that niche over the last 7 days (14 or 30 days, or the wider niche, when there are too few; it says which), with how many posts and creators used each, the median views of those posts and a link to an example post. It reads a stored sample that is refreshed weekly: it looks nothing up on TikTok, is not TikTok’s own trending list, and hashtags do not promise reach.

niche.description: The niche, sub-niche or topic in plain words, for example skincare, gym, TikTok Shop finds or personal finance. Text.

username.description: Optional. A public TikTok username, used only when no niche is given and that account was already read in the last 24 hours: the niche is then taken from its captions. Nothing is looked up on TikTok.

name: get_tiktok_trending_hashtags

hashtags.description: Hashtags used by 2 or more stored posts from 2 or more creators, most-used first (up to 15). Counts only.

example_url.description: The most-viewed stored post that used the hashtag: cite it as the source.

median_views.description: Median views of the posts that were stored WITH a view count. null = none was: say "no view count", never "0 views".

posts_with_views.description: How many of the posts using the hashtag were stored with a view count.

message.description: One or two plain sentences that say what was found or what went wrong.

status.description: ok, or the plain reason there is no result (not_found, private, no_videos, videos_unavailable, not_enough_videos, invalid_input, unknown_niche, niche_needed, no_data, rate_limited, paused, off, busy, unavailable).

window_days.description: 7, 14 or 30: how far back the stored posts go.

window_note.description: Which window was used and why. Say this to the person.

title: Trending TikTok hashtags in a niche
